newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada, land of the free -- and the burgled.
newsitem.headline: Canada, land of the free -- and the burgled.

text.p: Forget that image of safe Canada. Each year one crime is committed for every four or five Canadian households, a federal study showed on Wednesday.

The federal agency Statistics Canada said 2.88 million crimes were reported to police last year, and excluding traffic and drug crimes, 2.62 million were reported. Canada has 11.41 million households.

Go into most offices in Canadian cities and someone can probably recount a recent burglary or theft of some kind. The study counted 1.56 million such property crimes last year -- one in every seven households.
An Angus Reid poll taken for CTV News this week reported that one in four people surveyed had been a victim of a crime in the past two years, up from one in five in 1990.
Statistics Canada said violent crimes, mainly assaults, accounted for 291,000 incidents in 1996, though there were only 633 homicides during the entire year.
The overall level of reported crime declined by two percent from the year before, falling for the fifth consecutive year after almost three decades of steady increases.
Social scientists have postulated one possible reason for the decline -- the aging of Canada's population, since older people are less likely to commit crimes.
